stem: The potential energy φ (in joule) of a particle of mass 1 kg moving in the x–y plane obeys the law φ = 3x + 4y, where x and y are in metres. If the particle is at (6 m, 8 m) at time t = 0, then the work done by the conservative force on the particle from the initial position to the instant when it crosses the x-axis is (a) 25 J (b) −25 J (c) 50 J (d) −50 J —

Two blocks are connected to an ideal spring of stiffness 200 N/m. At a certain moment, the two blocks are moving in opposite directions with speeds 4 ms⁻¹ and 6 ms⁻¹, and the instantaneous elongation of the spring is 10 cm. The rate at which the spring energy (kx²/2) is increasing is (a) 500 J/s (b) 400 J/s (c) 200 J/s (d) 100 J/s —

The potential energy when a particle moves along the x axis is given by U(x) = 8x² + 2x⁴, where U is in joules and x is the coordinate of the particle in metres. The object exerting the force on the particle is very massive. If the total mechanical energy is 9.0 J, the limits of motion are: (a) −0.96 m, +0.96 m (b) −2.2 m, +2.2 m (c) −1.6 m, +1.6 m (d) −0.96 m, +2.2 m —
